title: Identification with the rational internal Hom and exceptional inverse image
statement:
In the rationalized constructible categories, the internal Hom
and exceptional inverse image agree with the operations defined
by coefficient passage in the manuscript. The integral tensor
product used for this passage is the completed derived tensor
product. In particular

$$
D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{X,E}),
\qquad
Rf_E^!M\cong D_{X,E}f^*D_{Y,E}M
$$

for every separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$. The functor
$Rf_E^!$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{!,E}$ on these
constructible categories, and $\omega_{X,E}=Ra_{X,E}^!E$.
These identifications preserve evaluations, units, and counits,
including under finite scalar extension.

source.place: node lem-coef-rational-operations, order 2152

proof.text: Use the inherited global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, $A_n=R/\pi^n$, and $\mathscr R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ on the small pro-etale site of $W$. In this proof an ambient integral tensor or internal Hom is over $\mathscr R_W$, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R_W$. Write $\mathcal C_R(W)=D^b_c(W,R)$ for the full derived-complete subcategory with constructible finite reductions and one uniform cohomological interval. Fix the small site skeletons and coefficient universes of the pro-etale site and size conventions, so the resolution and tower lemmas apply. All inverse limits below use strict towers and their functorial derived-limit realization. These are the coefficient categories and operations appearing in the statement.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: coefficient and tensor conventions

proof.text: For $P,K\in\mathcal C_R(X)$ let $N=P\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}K$. Choose K-flat resolutions with flat terms. Their tensor is K-flat: tensor an acyclic complex first with one resolution and then with the other, obtaining an acyclic complex twice by the definition of K-flatness. The K-flat change-of-rings lemma makes their reductions K-flat with flat terms as well; the strict completed-tensor construction descends independently of these choices by integral-operations well-definedness. Reassociation of their ordinary tensor complexes, $(p\otimes k)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(k\otimes a)$, identifies $N\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X$ with $P_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n$. For $m\le n$, further reduction is $P_m\otimes^L_{A_m}K_m$; all transition cocycles hold already on these tensor representatives. Thus this is a normalized DVR tower. The residue-Tor lemma supplies uniform finite Tor intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,d]$ for the inputs, and finite tensor preservation supplies constructibility and interval $[a+c,b+d]$. Taking the degree-zero test module $(A_n)_X$ in the definition of Tor amplitude shows that this same interval contains the cohomological support of every tensor reduction: tensor with the coefficient unit is identified with the original complex by $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Normalized effectivity identifies the reductions of its derived limit with these objects and makes the limit complete. Hence $C(N):=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(P_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n)$ belongs to $\mathcal C_R(X)$. By the definition of integral operations this is precisely $P\widehat\otimes_R^LK$. No assertion of local perfection on the site is used.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1-2: completed tensor and uniform intervals

proof.text: Use the strict K-flat tensor representative $Q$ of $N$ from Step 2. Its quotient maps $Q\to Q\otimes_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X$ commute strictly with the transitions. Since countable products are exact, the strict-tower limit is represented by the product mapping fiber of $1-s$. The quotient maps define a chain map $\eta_N:Q\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ with zero homotopy component. This is the canonical completion unit, natural in the strict representatives, not an arbitrary triangulated lift. Write $L_n=N\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X$. Normalized effectivity applied to the tower of Step 2 identifies the adjoint of the projection $C(N)\to\operatorname{Res}_nL_n$ with an isomorphism $e_n:C(N)\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_n)_X\to L_n$. The composite projection with $\eta_N$ is the reduction unit of $N$. By naturality and the triangle identity for derived extension/restriction, its adjoint is the identity on $L_n$; thus $e_n\circ(\eta_N\otimes^L(A_n)_X)=1_{L_n}$. Therefore $\eta_N$ is an isomorphism modulo every $\pi^n$.

source.place: Preserved blueprint_update.proof paragraphs 3-4: completion cone and its orthogonality; expanded using Stacks Tags 093M and 0149

proof.text: Let $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\eta_N)$. The coefficient ring $R$ is a DVR, hence a Noetherian domain. Flatness of $\mathscr R_X$ over the constant $R$-sheaf and its quotient identification imply that $\pi:\mathscr R_X\to\mathscr R_X$ is injective with cokernel $(A_1)_X$. Indeed multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on locally constant $R$-sections, and tensoring this injection with the flat completed sheaf preserves it. Consequently $F=[\mathscr R_X\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathscr R_X]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ resolves $(A_1)_X$. It is K-flat: tensoring any acyclic complex with $F$ gives a shifted multiplication cone, acyclic by the long exact cohomology sequence. Tensor with this two-term free complex commutes with mapping cones by the signed total-complex formula. Step 3 therefore gives $C\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}(A_1)_X=0$. But tensoring $C$ with $F$ also identifies this object with the cone of $\pi:C\to C$. Its vanishing and the long exact sequence show that $\pi$ induces isomorphisms on all cohomology objects, hence is invertible in the derived category.

source.place: Preserved blueprint_update.proof paragraphs 3-4: completion cone and its orthogonality; expanded using Stacks Tags 093M and 0149

proof.text:
For complete $M$, use its global Roos triangle from [def-weil-derived-complete], with terms $B=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_n M_n$. For every $j\in\mathbf Z$ and $h:C[j]\to\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$, scalar linearity gives $h\circ\pi_{C[j]}^n=\pi_{M_n}^n\circ h=0$, because $M_n$ is a complex of $(A_n)_X$-modules. The first factor is invertible by Step 4, so $h=0$. The categorical product property gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C[j],B)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(C[j],\operatorname{Res}_nM_n)=0$ for every $j$. Apply Hom-into-triangle exactness to the rotated Roos triangle $B[-1]\to M\to B$: its outer Hom groups vanish, since $\operatorname{Hom}(C[j],B[-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(C[j+1],B)=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(C[j],M)=0$ for all $j$. Finally Hom-out-of-triangle exactness on $N\xrightarrow{\eta_N}C(N)\to C\to N[1]$ and its rotations gives the natural $R$-linear bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C(N),M)\xrightarrow{\;\circ\eta_N\;}\operatorname{Hom}(N,M),$$
because the adjacent terms are $\operatorname{Hom}(C,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(C[-1],M)=0$. This proves the completion adjunction needed here using the global completeness definition itself.

source.place: Preserved blueprint_update.proof paragraphs 3-4: completion cone and its orthogonality; expanded using Stacks Tags 093M and 0149

proof.text:
The ambient tensor-Hom adjunction needed here is for an arbitrary ringed site. Choose K-flat representatives $Q_P,Q_K$ with flat terms and a K-injective representative $I_M$. The internal Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_K,I_M)$ is K-injective. The functorial total-complex currying isomorphism gives
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_P,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q_K,I_M))\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(Q_P\otimes Q_K),I_M).$$
These represent the corresponding derived internal Homs: the definition computes internal Hom into a K-injective resolution, and the cited quasi-isomorphism invariance permits the K-flat replacements. Taking degree-zero derived global sections and using the global-sections/Hom identification yields
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_X}K,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathscr R_X}(K,M)).$$
The currying formula sends a map $h$ to $p\mapsto(k\mapsto h(p\otimes k))$, where, for $p\in Q_P^i$, the tensor differential is $d(p\otimes k)=dp\otimes k+(-1)^ip\otimes dk$ and the differential of a homogeneous Hom map $h$ of degree $t$ is $dh=d_Mh-(-1)^thd$. Substitution in these two formulas verifies that currying commutes with the differential, with no additional sign in the displayed currying formula. Its inverse evaluates. This describes the evaluation and the naturality of the adjunction, rather than invoking a tensor-Hom theorem for scheme structure sheaves.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), and the proof of lemma-internal-hom immediately following 08JA

proof.text:
For $P,K,M\in\mathcal C_R(X)$, integral internal Hom is in $\mathcal C_R(X)$ by the integral-Hom preservation statement. Combine Steps 2-6, using fullness of this subcategory, to obtain the natural $R$-linear bijection
$$\Phi_R:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(P\widehat\otimes_R^LK,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(P,R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)).$$
Its left-to-right map is first precomposition with the canonical completion unit, then currying. The counit is the unique map $R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)\widehat\otimes_R^LK\to M$ whose precomposition with that unit is ambient evaluation. The unit is $\Phi_R(1_{P\widehat\otimes_R^LK}):P\to R\mathcal Hom_R(K,P\widehat\otimes_R^LK)$; the counit is $\Phi_R^{-1}(1_{R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)})$. Naturality of $\Phi_R$ makes the two triangle identities the assertion that currying and uncurrying are inverse. Thus completion has not silently changed the tensor adjunction or its evaluation.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 3-5: apply the completion adjunction to the ambient tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
The raw scalar localization has exactly the same objects and Hom groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(U,V)\otimes_RE$. Tensoring $\Phi_R$ with $E$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,E)}(P\otimes_E^LK,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,E)}(P,R\mathcal Hom_E(K,M)).$$
Every map is a finite sum of integral maps times scalars; the displayed bijection sends $h\otimes a$ to $\Phi_R(h)\otimes a$. Its naturality for fractions follows from $R$-linearity: the two sides of each integral naturality identity are multiplied by the same product of the denominators' inverses. In two-variable operations $u\otimes a$ and $v\otimes b$ act by the integral operation on $(u,v)$ times $ab$ (precomposition in the contravariant variable). Thus these are exactly the coefficient-passage functors, on maps as well as objects. The evaluation, unit, counit and their identities are the integral ones tensored with $1$, as follows by applying this Hom bijection to identities. No new objects from a Karoubi envelope are involved.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 5-6: scalar-localized Hom bijection and its evaluation

proof.text: Integral Verdier duality is $D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,\omega_{X,R})$ and the rational duality functor is its localization, with $\omega_{X,E}$ the image of $\omega_{X,R}$. Specialize Step 8 to that second argument. It gives the asserted equality $D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{X,E})$, with evaluation the rationalized integral evaluation. The double-dual map is the same one as in rational Verdier duality, since both are obtained by transposing that evaluation; the cited integral and rational duality statements identify these actual maps.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 6: specialize internal Hom to the dualizing object

proof.text: For separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, put $A_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and $G_R(M)=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_n^!M_n$. The integral exceptional-adjoint theorem supplies the adjunction $A_R\dashv G_R$ on the stated bounded constructible categories, its actual unit $\eta_R$, counit $\varepsilon_R$, and the canonical isomorphism $G_R\cong D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}$ identifying those data. The compact-support functor is $R$-linear by its coefficient-level construction and strict derived limit. The displayed formula for $G_R$ also makes it $R$-linear: internal duality acts by linear precomposition (Steps 6 and 9), completed pullback is linear on the coefficient representatives of Step 1, and the formula contains two dualities. For $h:A_RK\to M$, its adjoint is $G_R(h)\circ\eta_{R,K}$, so the adjoint of $ah$ is $G_R(ah)\circ\eta_{R,K}=a(G_R(h)\circ\eta_{R,K})$. This proves the required linearity of the actual adjunction bijection. Apply scalar transport to the functors and natural transformations, and explicitly tensor the integral Hom bijection with $E$. This gives $A_E\dashv G_E$, with units $\eta_R\otimes1$ and counits $\varepsilon_R\otimes1$; the triangle equations remain equations after tensoring with $1$. The transport statement alone is not being used as a theorem asserting that every adjunction survives an unspecified localization.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 7: localize the integral exceptional adjunction

proof.text: The left adjoint $A_E$ of Step 10 is the rational compact-support functor: its integral representative and strict finite-reduction tower are exactly the ones in the definition of rational compact support. Likewise $G_E$ is the rationalized finite-stage exceptional inverse image specified in the exceptional-inverse-image definition. Localizing the integral formula, using the already identified pullback and duality functors, gives $Rf_E^!M\cong D_{X,E}f^*D_{Y,E}M$. If either operation is instead characterized by the adjunction, its comparison is forced by the counit: the unique map between right adjoints whose transpose is the other counit is inverse to the reverse comparison, since both composites transpose to the original counit. This proves preservation of the units and counits too. For $f=a_X$, the integral theorem identifies $G_R(R)$ with $\omega_{X,R}$, so rationalizing gives $Ra_{X,E}^!E=\omega_{X,E}$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 7: identify the prescribed operations, formula and structure-morphism value

proof.text: We now check finite extension, including the adjunction maps. Let $E\subset L$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, $v=\varpi_L$, ramification index $e$, and $r=[L:E]$. At level $n$ use $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, finite free over $A_n$; these are the specified cofinal $S$-levels. Write $T_W$ for integral completed extension. Finite-free completed-scalar comparison identifies it, by its canonical completion map, with ordinary derived extension $-\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_W}\mathscr S_W$, where $\mathscr S_W$ is finite free of rank $r$ over $\mathscr R_W$. This comparison is between the actual strict-tower functors, not just unrelated objects with isomorphic reductions. The integral dualizing, internal-Hom and duality comparisons $u,v_{K,M},\beta$ preserve evaluation and biduality; pullback and tensor also have the stated scalar comparisons. In particular internal-Hom evaluation has the scalar rule $(h\otimes s,k\otimes t)\mapsto h(k)\otimes st$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8: use finite free extension, not arbitrary infinite coefficient extension

proof.text:
Fix one compactification $f=pj$ at all coefficient levels. The compact-support reduction-tower functor gives a lift to the derived category of strict towers, whose evaluations and quotient transitions are exactly the stated finite compact-support functors; use this lift when applying derived inverse limit below. At $A_n\to B_n$, extension by zero commutes with finite direct sums and restriction of scalars because it is an exact additive left adjoint computed degreewise. The $Rp_*$ finite-free comparison is the one in the finite-free-extension statement, and composing gives $T_{Y,n}Rf_{!,A_n}\cong Rf_{!,B_n}T_{X,n}$. These maps are compatible with the quotient transitions: restriction of scalars commutes with $Rf_!$, and the cited finite-free comparisons commute with reductions. Choose an $R$-basis of $S$, giving a compatible basis of every $B_n$. On the underlying $A_n$-complexes the comparison is the finite-sum map $(Rf_{!,A_n}K_n)^{\oplus r}\to Rf_{!,A_n}(K_n^{\oplus r})$. A basis change acts by the same matrix on both sides, so the map is independent of the basis. Finite sums commute with termwise products and $1-s$ and hence with the strict-tower cone computing $R\lim$; exact countable products justify this model on pro-etale modules. Taking these actual tower maps and the cofinal levels of Step 12 yields
$$\alpha:T_Y A_R\xrightarrow{\sim}A_S T_X.$$
Its underlying map in any basis is finite-sum distributivity. All its inverses and compositions are therefore compatible with the chosen reduction maps, not just identifiable after reduction.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: finite-free compact-support comparison on strict coefficient towers

proof.text:
Let $U_W$ be restriction from $\mathscr S_W$ to $\mathscr R_W$; it leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged and is exact. The balanced maps $h\mapsto[k\mapsto h(1\otimes k)]$ and $g\mapsto[s\otimes k\mapsto s g(k)]$ give $T_W\dashv U_W$ on module sheaves. Finite freeness makes $T_W$ exact as well. Thus the partial-derived-adjunction lemma applies with everywhere-defined derived functors: their quasi-isomorphism diagrams are already constant up to the invertible images of the quasi-isomorphisms. It gives the same adjunction on ambient derived categories. It restricts to the constructible categories. Indeed $T_W$ preserves them by the integral finite-extension statement. For $N\in\mathcal C_S(W)$, choose an $S$-K-flat resolution; it is also $R$-K-flat: for an acyclic $R$-complex $Q$, first tensor with the finite free $\mathscr S_W$, then with the $S$-K-flat resolution. Both operations preserve the required acyclicity. Tensoring this representative gives
$$(U_WN)\otimes^L_{\mathscr R_W}(A_n)_W=\operatorname{Res}_{A_n\to B_n}(N\otimes^L_{\mathscr S_W}(B_n)_W).$$
Restriction preserves finite-level constructibility (finite modules remain finite, and the same local constant presentations apply) and the given uniform cohomological interval. It also commutes with products and cones on the underlying sheaves. Completeness therefore follows from the complete $S$-tower on the cofinal $en$ levels of Step 12. Hence $U_WN\in\mathcal C_R(W)$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded using Tag 0DVC (derived-lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors): finite-free extension/restriction adjunction and its domain

proof.text:
Apply Steps 10 and 14 over both rings. For $N\in\mathcal C_S(Y)$ the following natural bijections, in this order, determine an isomorphism $\rho:U_XG_SN\cong G_RU_YN$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,U_XG_SN)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(T_XK,G_SN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(A_ST_XK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(T_YA_RK,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(A_RK,U_YN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,G_RU_YN).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle map is precomposition with $\alpha_K$. Taking identities on the two representing objects gives inverse comparison maps: their composites are identities because the displayed bijections are inverse and natural. In particular this uses only the constructible exceptional adjunction, not an unbounded ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: explicit Hom bijections defining the right-adjoint comparison

proof.text:
Define $b_M:T_XG_RM\to G_ST_YM$ as the transpose under $A_S\dashv G_S$ of
$$A_ST_XG_RM\xrightarrow{\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}}T_YA_RG_RM\xrightarrow{T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}}T_YM.$$
This map is invertible. To check it, choose the basis of Step 13. Then $U_YT_YM=M^{\oplus r}$, and $\rho$ of Step 15 identifies the underlying target with $G_R(M^{\oplus r})$. A right adjoint preserves finite products; here they are finite biproducts. The $i$-th component of $\rho U_Xb_M$ is $G_R$ applied to the $i$-th coefficient projection, composed with the map transposed from the corresponding component of $T_Y\varepsilon_R$. By the scalar rule for the extension/restriction adjunction and the finite-sum description of $\alpha$, this is projection onto the $i$-th copy of $G_RM$, followed by $G_R\varepsilon_R\circ\eta_RG_R=1$. The off-diagonal components are zero. Thus the underlying matrix of $b_M$ is the identity on $(G_RM)^{\oplus r}$. Restriction detects an isomorphism, since it leaves the cohomology sheaves of its cone unchanged. This proves invertibility without inferring equality of maps from equality of their finite reductions.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: finite-free mate isomorphism; finite products from Tag 0038 (categories-lemma-adjoint-exact)

proof.text:
Apply the mate counit identity [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] and unit identity [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] to $L_1=A_R$, $R_1=G_R$, $L_2=A_S$, $R_2=G_S$, $G=T_X$, $H=T_Y$, and the square $\alpha^{-1}$. Step 16 defined $b$ by exactly this transpose. Hence
$$\varepsilon_{S,T_YM}\circ A_S(b_M)\circ\alpha_{G_RM}=T_Y(\varepsilon_{R,M}),$$
$$b_{A_RK}\circ T_X(\eta_{R,K})=G_S(\alpha_K^{-1})\circ\eta_{S,T_XK}.$$
These are the required counit and unit identities for the actual integral adjunctions. The only rearrangement is precomposition of the counit equation with the isomorphism $\alpha_{G_RM}$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: mate equations for units and counits and the duality formula

proof.text: The integral adjunction uses the coherent finite exceptional realization specified in [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Apply [lem-coef-finite-scalar-mate-realization] with the fixed compactification of Step 13 and the cofinal $S$-levels $en$ of Step 12. Its source and target comparisons are precisely those used in Steps 12-14. It identifies the total limit of the finite transposes with the map whose transpose is $T_Y\varepsilon_R\circ\alpha^{-1}$. That map is $b$ by Step 16 and injectivity of the adjunction bijection. Thus the coefficient-passage exceptional comparison is $b$, with the equations of Step 17. No equality of integral maps is inferred solely from equality of their finite reductions.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: mate equations for units and counits and the duality formula

proof.text:
Write $c_Z:T_Xf_R^*Z\xrightarrow{\sim}f_S^*T_YZ$ and $\beta^W_Z:T_WD_{W,R}Z\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{W,S}T_WZ$ for the pullback and duality comparisons of Step 12. With the canonical formula identifications $\kappa_R:G_R\cong D_{X,R}f_R^*D_{Y,R}$ and $\kappa_S:G_S\cong D_{X,S}f_S^*D_{Y,S}$, their composite is
$$b'_M=\kappa_{S,T_YM}^{-1}\circ D_{X,S}\bigl(c_{D_{Y,R}M}^{-1}\circ f_S^*((\beta^Y_M)^{-1})\bigr)\circ\beta^X_{f_R^*D_{Y,R}M}\circ T_X(\kappa_{R,M}).$$
The arrow inside $D_{X,S}$ runs from $f_S^*D_{Y,S}T_YM$ to $T_Xf_R^*D_{Y,R}M$, as contravariance requires. By [lem-coef-dual-formula-scalar-transpose], the $A_S\dashv G_S$ transpose of this map is $T_Y\varepsilon_R\circ\alpha^{-1}$. It equals the defining transpose of $b$ in Step 16, so $b'=b$. Consequently the formula comparison preserves the same units and counits as the coefficient-passage comparison; the evaluation comparisons remain those fixed in Step 12.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 8, expanded: mate equations for units and counits and the duality formula

proof.text: Finally rationalize the finite-extension comparisons. By the definition of $-\otimes_E L$, its integral representative is exactly $T$, and each component of $\alpha,b,u,v,\beta$ is sent to that component tensored with $1$. Composition in raw scalar localization is bilinear, so both equations of Step 17 and the evaluation identities remain the same equations after localization. Coherence for $E\subset L\subset L'$ follows at compact support from multiplication $(k\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto k\otimes st$ on the finite free tower maps; taking mates gives the same equality for $b$ because their transposes are the same composite counit. For internal Hom and duality, identity and associator coherence are those of the integral comparisons. The rational duality theorem gives the corresponding evaluation and biduality comparisons as well. This proves every scalar-extension compatibility claimed in the item within the specified rationalized constructible categories.

source.place: Proof, final two paragraphs: rationalize the specified comparisons and their equations

blueprint_update.statement:
In the rationalized constructible categories, the internal Hom
and exceptional inverse image agree with the operations defined
by coefficient passage. The integral tensor
product used for this passage is the completed derived tensor
product. In particular

$$
D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_{X,E}),
\qquad
Rf_E^!M\cong D_{X,E}f^*D_{Y,E}M
$$

for every separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$. The functor
$Rf_E^!$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{!,E}$ on these
constructible categories, and $\omega_{X,E}=Ra_{X,E}^!E$.
These identifications preserve evaluations, units, and counits,
including under finite scalar extension.

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/\pi^n$.
For integral constructible $P,K$, their completed tensor is

$$
P\widehat\otimes_R^LK
=R\varprojlim_n(P_n\otimes_{A_n}^LK_n).
$$

The input reductions have uniform Tor intervals by
[lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. Finite tensor preservation
[lem-sf-tensor-ctf] gives constructible tensor reductions
with the sum of those intervals. Tensor associativity makes
this a normalized tower, so
[lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] gives precisely these
reductions of the displayed complete object. It is therefore
an object of the integral constructible category.

Here is the completion adjunction needed to use ambient
tensor–Hom adjunction. For any ambient $R$-complex $N$,
set $\widehat N=R\varprojlim_n(N\otimes_R^LA_n)$.
The same effectivity lemma, which does not require boundedness,
shows that the canonical map $N\to\widehat N$ is an
isomorphism modulo every $\pi^n$. Its cone $C$ has
$C\otimes_R^LA_1=0$. The two-term free resolution of
$A_1$ shows that multiplication by $\pi$ on $C$ is
invertible. For a complete $M$, write
$M=R\varprojlim_n M_n$ as in
[def-weil-derived-complete]. The derived mapping complex
$R\operatorname{Hom}(C,M_n)$ is zero: multiplication by
$\pi$ is invertible through its first argument, whereas
$\pi^n$ is zero through its second argument. Since mapping
into a derived limit preserves that limit,
$R\operatorname{Hom}(C,M)=0$. Thus

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}(\widehat N,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}(N,M).
$$

This proves the required left-adjoint property of completion
directly for the completed coefficient sheaf used here.

Integral internal Hom preserves $D^b_c$ by
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom]. Localize its functor in
both arguments and localize completed tensor product. Apply
the just proved completion adjunction to $N=P\otimes_R^LK$
and the complete integral representative $M$. Ambient
tensor–Hom adjunction then gives

$$
\Hom(P\widehat\otimes_R^LK,M)\otimes_RE
\cong
\Hom(P,R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M))\otimes_RE.
$$

By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], these are exactly
the Hom groups in the rationalized category. Naturality for
fractional morphisms follows by linearity. This identifies the
localized internal Hom with the coefficient-passage operation of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], including its
evaluation. With $M=\omega$ it gives the first formula and
the functor of [thm-coef-rational-verdier].

The integral exceptional adjunction, its units and counits, and
the integral formula $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$ are
[prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Localize their
Hom-group adjunction by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].
The localized left adjoint is precisely the compact-support
functor in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].
The right adjoint is therefore the operation characterized in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; uniqueness of a right
adjoint with its counit identifies the localized formula and all
its adjunction data. Taking $f=a_X$ gives the dualizing-object
identification.

For finite scalar extension, compact support commutes with the
finite free coefficient tensor: at finite levels this is the
projection comparison for a finite sum of the coefficient unit,
and finite free tensor commutes with the derived limit defining
integral compact support. The comparisons of
[lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] and coefficient
compatibility of pullback give the corresponding comparison for
$D_Xf^*D_Y$. Transposing it through the integral adjunction
identifies it with the mate of that compact-support comparison:
the adjunction formula uses exactly the evaluations and counits
preserved by the duality comparisons. Thus the units and
counits agree under finite extension as well as under
rationalization.

This proof is an identification inside the
specified constructible coefficient categories; it does not
replace scalar localization by an assertion that internal Hom
commutes with an arbitrary infinite coefficient extension on the
whole ambient derived category of sheaves.
